subject: Error in truncation on dlm, state space modeling.

messages.author: 67f4b9053b39c847
messages.subject: Error in truncation on dlm, state space modeling.
parts:
hi
I am trying to simulate following model about dlm, and want to truncate parameter a2[each] inthe system equation part.
==
data{
  int T;
  vector[T] Y;
  vector[T] X1;
  vector[T] X2;
}
parameters{
  vector<lower=0>[T] bl;
  vector<lower=0>[T] a1;
  vector<lower=0>[T] a2;

  real<lower=0> obs_Y;
  real<lower=0> sn_bl;
  real<lower=0> sn_a1;
  real<lower=0> sn_a2;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[T] Yp;
  # linear predictor
  Yp <- bl + a1 .* X1 + a2 .* X2;

}
model{
  #obs equation
  Y ~ normal(Yp,obs_Y);

  # system  equation
  for(t in 2:T){
    bl[t] ~ normal(bl[t-1],sn_bl);
    a1[t] ~ normal(a1[t-1],sn_a1);
    a2[t] ~ normal(a2[t-1],sn_a2)T[,a1[t]];
  }
}
==
but I got an error message
--
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'model' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Initialization failed after 100 attempts.  Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done
--
Modeling was succeeded in case that I got rid of truncation from system equation.
And I tried 3 alternatives
 ・specifying initial values
 ・reducing ranges of constrained values
 ・reparameterizing the model
as this error massage shows.

Anyway, our purpose is to restrict the relation about size between two parameters a1 and a2.
All of my idea have been failed, somebody ,, please let me know how to sort out this problem.. 

==
Hiroki Mizukami

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error in truncation on dlm, state space modeling.
parts:
In Stan, the support of the model needs to match the
constraints on the parameters. And initial values need
to satisfy the constraints, which will be automatic if
you define the constraints to match the model support and
then use random initialization.

In this case you have

parameters {
...
vector<lower=0>[T] a2;
...
model {
...
a2[t] ~ normal(a2[t-1],sn_a2)T[,a1[t]];

The problem is that a2 is declared with only the constraint that
a2[t] > 0, but then the support for a2[t] is truncated above at a1[t].

You can code this up in Stan using
an array of positive ordered types.

positive_ordered[2] a[T];

which guarantees that a[t,2] > a[t,1] > 0.

Note that this is backward from the way you wrote it so that

a[t,1] ==your== a2[t]

a[t,2] ==your== a1[t]

then you can just write

for (t in 2:T) {
a[t,1] ~ normal(a[t-1,1],sn_a1);
a[t,2] ~ normal(a[t-1,2],sn_a2);
}

without the truncation constraint. Note that the sn_a1 and sn_a2 will
also be reversed. I'd have just implemented sn_a1 and sn_a2 as
a 2-vector, and then the loop looks like:

for (t in 2:T)
for (i in 1:2)
a[t,i] ~ normal(a[t-1,i], sn_a[i]);

You could then make things more efficient by vectorizing.

You might also put priors on bl[1], a1[1] or a2[1], and on the sn.

- Bob

The problem has gone!

Actually , I deal with it by followings,

parameters{
...
  positive_ordered[2] a[T];
...
}
transformed parameters{
...
  vector[T] a1;
  vector[T] a2;

  for(t in 1:T){
    a1[t] <- a[t,1];
    a2[t] <- a[t,2];
  }
}

==
Vectorizing is useful, but we have to gave the variable name explicitly , to understand the meaning of variables.
 I really really appreciate you! thanks!

Hiroki Mizukami

parts:
On Jul 27, 2014, at 10:22 PM, Hiroki Mizukami <rocky...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Bob
>
> The problem has gone!
Glad to hear it.

> Actually , I deal with it by followings,
>
> parameters{
> ...
> positive_ordered[2] a[T];
> ...
> }
> transformed parameters{
> ...
> vector[T] a1;
> vector[T] a2;
>
> for(t in 1:T){
> a1[t] <- a[t,1];
> a2[t] <- a[t,2];
> }
> }
>
> ==
> Vectorizing is useful, but we have to gave the variable name explicitly , to understand the meaning of variables.

I don't see why. a[,1] is just a2 and a[,2] is just your a1.
So it's not like they're getting lost. Just renamed.

If you want to recover the a1 and a2 as above, then it's more
efficient to do it in the generated quantities block instead of
the transformed parameters block. The issue with making it transformed
parameters is that it negatively impacts speed because any parameters,
including transformed parameters, get added to the expression graph for
the log probability and take up time during gradient calculations (here,
needless applications of the chain rule).

But, if you want to use a1 and a2 in the model, then they need to be
transformed parameters.

> I really really appreciate you! thanks!
>

You're welcome!

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error in truncation on dlm, state space modeling.
parts:
Hi Hiroki,

As Bob mentioned, if you just want to pick out the T-dimensional vector from ordered[2] a[T] it'll be much faster doing that in the "generated quantities" block instead of the "transformed parameters" block. All that means is you'll want to define a1 and a2 inside the generated quantities block and do the assignment there.

You're right that Stan doesn't have a good way of accessing a[,1] or a[,2].

Regarding vectorization:
- for loops in Stan are not slow.
- vectorization is faster in Stan when it can figure out how to not calculate expressions multiple times and/or it has special implementation that reduces the time it takes for automatic differentiation. The place where Stan does this the best is in its probability distributions.
- vectorization is convenient for writing out expressions

I guess the point I want to make is that the loops aren't slow in Stan and you should just use loops to set a1 and a2 without worry about trying to find a more efficient way to do it.



Daniel
